title: Test craft
description: How to design tests that stay fast, readable and meaningful.

rules.title: Design before writing
rules.text: Before writing a test, decide what the module is for, its input and output contract and the failure it guards against.

rules.title: Cheapest sufficient level
rules.text: Pick the cheapest test level that reproduces the risk, and use an end-to-end path for user-visible behavior.

rules.title: Reuse before creating
rules.text: Extend existing test files, fixtures and helpers before creating new ones.

rules.title: Assert behavior
rules.text: Assert observable behavior through public interfaces, and let the test name say why it matters.

rules.title: No logic in tests
rules.text: Do not put conditionals or loops in tests. Split the test or parametrize the cases.

rules.title: Parametrize duplicates
rules.text: Merge near-duplicate tests into one parameterized test with named cases.

rules.title: Assert the whole shape
rules.text: Assert the whole result shape or a snapshot rather than one field when the shape is the contract.

rules.title: No coverage padding
rules.text: Do not add trivial tests only to raise the coverage number.

rules.title: Fast and deterministic
rules.text: Keep tests fast and deterministic. Prefer in-memory execution, and use threads or subprocesses only when nothing else works.

rules.title: Wait on conditions
rules.text: Wait on a condition, never on a fixed sleep.

rules.title: Fixtures stay read-only
rules.text: Never modify committed fixtures from a test. Copy them to a temporary directory first.

rules.title: Real over mocks
rules.text: Prefer real objects or small fakes over mocks. When a mock is unavoidable, document why.

rules.title: Mirror the source tree
rules.text: Mirror the source tree in the test tree so tests are easy to find.

rules.title: Offline unit tests
rules.text: Unit tests must not touch the network. Isolate them from environment variables that enable tracing or real services.

rules.title: Plain test names
rules.text: Name tests after the behavior and omit "should". Keep each test body short.
